G4 has no existing spec criterion and no existing test. The pieces a new test would reuse are in the engine's test helpers.

- **`test-suite.spec.md`**
  - TST-B5 (lines 35-40) gives each test its own temporary folder, home folder and state root.
  - TST-AC6 (line 55) covers two concurrent tests.
  - TST-AC7 (line 56) covers only "after a full run" of the suite.
  - Nothing there mentions a package's own test run, a start from a package folder, or the machine index.
  - The Purpose (line 5) says the tests are "started with `python -m pytest` in the engine folder".
  - `spec.rule.md` allows at most 3 scenarios per behaviour and no fixture names.
- **`workspace-and-concurrency.spec.md`**: WSP-AC2 (line 165) says only that a test session fails if a test leaves state in the real state root.
- **`engine/tests/test_suite_isolation.py`** (read, 60 lines)
  - It holds the two tests for TST-AC6 and TST-AC7. Both return at once when `is_nested()`.
  - The TST-AC7 test (lines 53-59) takes `real_folders_snapshot()`, runs `nested_pytest(*SAMPLE_TEST_FILES)` and asserts `changed_paths(before, after) == []`.
  - The TST-AC6 test (lines 37-50) shows how to run a module outside the engine folder: `nested_pytest(..., scratch=True)`.
  - No test starts a fixture package's tests from that package's folder.
- **`engine/tests/conftest.py`** (read)
  - Lines 41-54: the autouse `_isolated_home` fixture sets `TEMPERGRAPH_HOME` to a temporary folder, sets `TEMPERGRAPH_LOOP=off` and removes the state-root and session variables. It applies only to this suite.
  - Lines 126-139: `nested_pytest` runs `python -m pytest -c <engine pyproject>` with `cwd=ENGINE_ROOT`.
    - With `scratch=True` it loads `conftest,tests.conftest` through `PYTEST_PLUGINS`.
    - It has no `cwd` parameter, so a run from a package folder needs a new argument or a new helper.
  - Lines 170-179: `real_folders_snapshot()` takes the repository files and, when no engine drives the session, `stat_tree(Path.home()/".tempergraph")` and the state root. The home snapshot would include a machine index kept under `~/.tempergraph`, but the code has no separate "machine index" snapshot.
  - Lines 195-200: `changed_paths`.
  - Lines 203-219: the session start and finish hooks fail the session if the real folders changed.
- **Not found**
  - A fixture package for such a test: the engine tests may not name a workflow, and `workflow_packages()` at conftest.py lines 24-27 only finds real packages.
  - Any entry point that would make the isolation load without a package fixture.

New text would go into `test-suite.spec.md` as a TST-B5 extension or a new behaviour, plus a TST-AC9 criterion. The test belongs in `test_suite_isolation.py`, carrying that id.

ARTIFACT gap_finding: No spec criterion or test covers a package's own test run: test-suite.spec.md TST-B5 (l.35-40), TST-AC6/AC7 (l.55-56) and Purpose (l.5) cover only the engine's suite started in the engine folder, and workspace-and-concurrency.spec.md WSP-AC2 (l.165) covers only the real state root. The existing proof is tests/test_suite_isolation.py: l.53-59 (TST-AC7: real_folders_snapshot, nested_pytest(*SAMPLE_TEST_FILES), assert changed_paths == []) and l.37-50 (TST-AC6, nested_pytest scratch=True with a module outside the engine folder). Reusable parts, all in tests/conftest.py (read): nested_pytest l.126-139 (cwd fixed to ENGINE_ROOT, no cwd parameter, so a package-folder start needs a new argument or helper), real_folders_snapshot l.170-179 (repo files, stat_tree of ~/.tempergraph, real state root; home and state root skipped when TEMPERGRAPH_SESSION_KEY is set), changed_paths l.195-200, the guard hooks l.203-219 and the autouse _isolated_home fixture l.41-54 (engine suite only). No separate machine-index snapshot exists; the home tree stands in for it. No fixture package exists, and workflow_packages() l.24-27 finds only real ones, so a new test must build a scratch fixture package and must not name a workflow. New text would extend TST-B5 or add a TST-B behaviour plus a TST-AC9 in test-suite.spec.md; the test belongs in test_suite_isolation.py, carrying that id.
